## Design

### 2026-10-05 – First thing I did was research: I learned a lot about the different parts that Ill soon be using this includes the BMP280, MPU6050, and the ESP32, with and SD card as the logger. I want to get directi

**5h**

First thing I did was research: I learned a lot about the different parts that Ill soon be using this includes the BMP280, MPU6050, and the ESP32, with and SD card as the logger. I want to get direction, position, temperature, and more and these two sensors do a lot of that, and they also are fairly simple to code.

![Screenshot 2026-10-05 225141](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/PyBRq8PPAIR10a85zVadomccKWQcxryn/455a0e1126f2a7320113692a9701460a6937b47e83d3fe9ac956c9aebbe67fc8.png)

Then after this I finally got the KiCad downloaded and spent some time learning how to use KiCad since I had absolutely no clue on what to do, like footprints and pinouts and stuff.

![Screenshot 2026-10-05 225334](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/PyBRq8PPAIR10a85zVadomccKWQcxryn/46135fc92019d34dab1b86ad86ef4e15cd6ea2ee639ccf79e0f30acea6d679a7.png)

After doing that I learned a good amount of KiCad schematic drawing to import the boards that I need, these include of ESP32-WROOM-32E, found that this one was simple to use and quick to learn since I have already done a lot of building stuff with the ESP32, this was just my first time learning about the PCB side of things. Also included the BMP280 and MPU-6050. Also, with the addition of the Micro_SD_Card_Det1, i only need one detector pin more than that it just becomes a little too complicated for me so let's keep it chill.

![Screenshot 2026-10-05 224937](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/PyBRq8PPAIR10a85zVadomccKWQcxryn/c2336ef47b3e8676ec4d97c92765ce59b74562f2f23df2335b76147a51790596.png)

After learning all of that goofy stuff I moved on to making the wires, it's kind of weird to draw them so it took me a good amount of time to even do this simple thing which I should probably ger faster at which would be beneficial.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/PyBRq8PPAIR10a85zVadomccKWQcxryn/34f59dab1e8572276ca33369a456eef8c11691708c52b3ca63fbb2b316d3fe7d.png)

Then I found out that I kind of need a switch to make sure that the power doesn't connect immediately and so I put a switch there just to make sure like if there was a short circuit, hopefully no magic smoke will arise. At this time, I found out you could name the board, I named it Akasha, in my language this means sky, and since it's a flight computer well, they go hand in hand really nicely and so the name was giving Akasha Flight Computer! I actually really like the name its suppppppppppppppper tuff.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/PyBRq8PPAIR10a85zVadomccKWQcxryn/bac5f59184add7c9690c7e2b6a473a68bdb00dd553046a71df77edd4fc642020.png)

### 2026-10-07 – So well, if you haven't seen my reel yet, I'm trying to build a flight computer. Right now, I figured out that you need a battery (WOW!). For this I decided to use a screw terminal since its strong, i

**11h**

So well, if you haven't seen my reel yet, I'm trying to build a flight computer. Right now, I figured out that you need a battery (WOW!). For this I decided to use a screw terminal since its strong, it works well and it also me to feel good when I use it and to make sure that I don't lose valuable data just cause of a disconnected battery.

![Screenshot 2026-10-06 221448](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/PyBRq8PPAIR10a85zVadomccKWQcxryn/029c96cf0544cce01f1b674ecc92ffda8c1150b9630d60199437467c41bc0115.png)

After this I used a AP63203 DC to DC buck converter, the reason behind this is because I found out that the ESP need 3.3v and outputs a 3.3v logic for the sensors, and so what I did was to make a decision between over volting or under volting the board so I decided to go with 4 AA batteries means 1.5v * 4 which 6v, that would be bad to directly connect to the ESP so that's why there is a buck converter and this converts it to a fixed 3.3v.

![Screenshot 2026-10-06 222736](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/PyBRq8PPAIR10a85zVadomccKWQcxryn/e8b7040e49cecd285b1e6a0abd1f1f91d35186a023544f4c856218b4c5dcbd16.png)

Now I decided to wire the MP6050 and I also made a quick key that just makes it easier to view and helps me in the long run.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/PyBRq8PPAIR10a85zVadomccKWQcxryn/fdb6e6618831fab4634595fd64dc77ce03a48d02ca811d196b4ddfacd95145de.png)

This is the image of the wiring of the MPU6050, the main ones are SDA SCL which are the ones that a needed mostly the other ones can be whatever.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/PyBRq8PPAIR10a85zVadomccKWQcxryn/8b90d1e1c9ff02d8290542824191cb69c9449094e5ab4ec1eba6cf1a76444270.png)

WRONG! WRONG! WRONG! The other wires do not go anywhere they want the other ones are used for smoothing voltage and stuff as you can see, I used capacitors and I also used and inductor for the Buck converter. You can see down below!

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/PyBRq8PPAIR10a85zVadomccKWQcxryn/763904e1e5b15085985c84c624f832b1ae20921cf119ab7bc92f61b802e63b7f.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/PyBRq8PPAIR10a85zVadomccKWQcxryn/dd1db383fe32e658997c93fce379616c584876781ee475efec13fe1968187cac.png)

These were done mainly so that there wouldn't be weird voltage jumps and drops and so that led to the large amount of capacitor as you see above.

And so this led to the final board AT THE MOMENT, soon I will add the BMP, its capacitors and everything need soon after and you see below.

![Screenshot 2026-10-06 225111](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/PyBRq8PPAIR10a85zVadomccKWQcxryn/61dd72374861eae0d2a297b0141d7d9f43b1e4464e8f95a7a211e7a46cafc7c1.png)

Now I have also wired the BMP280 to the board this one actually didn't need pull up resistors... I think, but we'll see if it doesn't work out and so here's the wiring for the BMP

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/PyBRq8PPAIR10a85zVadomccKWQcxryn/adf7060c14c5d2e4d20e2c9901e2065be2f0c20556d9eaa0e48685eba825839a.png)
